difficulty_reason: In Situation labelled situation-free-at-generic-points the lemma asserts that for each p >= 0 the functor H_p of equation labelled equation-free-at-generic-points is representable by a locally closed immersion S_p -> S, and that S_p -> S is of finite presentation when F is of finite presentation (statement lines 7630-7637). The proof treats all p concurrently for a fixed S: H_p is an fppf sheaf by Lemma labelled lemma-free-at-generic-points, so by Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-descent-data-sheaves, More on Morphisms, Lemma labelled more-morphisms-lemma-separated-locally-quasi-finite-morphisms-fppf-descend and Descent, Lemma labelled descent-lemma-descending-fppf-property-immersion the question is etale local, hence Zariski local, on S (proof lines 7639-7647). Writing xi_s for the generic point of the fibre X_s, generic flatness gives that F_s is locally free of some rank p(s) near xi_s, and p(s) is computed as the dimension of the fibre of F at xi_s, so H_{p(s)}(s) is nonempty and H_q(s) is empty for q different from p(s) (proof lines 7649-7663). Because f is smooth hence open, one may replace X by any open U without changing H_p, and after shrinking to a neighbourhood where F is generated by p(s) elements via a surjection O_X^{p(s)} -> F, the functor H_{p(s)} is identified with the functor F_iso of equation labelled equation-iso, which Theorem labelled theorem-flattening-map represents by a closed immersion (proof lines 7665-7698). The global representability then follows formally by induction on the maximum of p(s): representability for the maximum is a closed immersion, and removing S_p lowers the maximum by at least one (proof lines 7700-7709). The finite presentation statement is obtained by redoing the induction and checking that each complement stays quasi-compact, which uses that S_p -> S is a closed immersion of finite presentation (proof lines 7711-7725). Converting the local closed-immersion statement into a global locally closed immersion by induction on the maximal rank is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
